newsitem.title: USA: TWA says FBI comments on crash put answer no closer.
newsitem.headline: TWA says FBI comments on crash put answer no closer.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc. said Monday that comments made over the weekend by FBI officials about the likely cause of the crash of TWA Flight 800 "move us no closer to an answer than we were yesterday or last week or at this time last month."
"A conclusion based on ...'the evidence we have not found' ... is clearly no conclusion at all," the airline said in a prepared statement responding to the officials' remarks.
FBI Director Louis Freeh, on the NBC television broadcast "Meet the Press" on Sunday, said mechanical failure likely brought down TWA Flight 800 last July.
"I think that the evidence as we've developed it to date ... would lead the inquiry toward the conclusion that this was a catastrophic mechanical failure," Freeh said.
He said neither the FBI nor the National Transportation Safety Board had reached a formal conclusion on the midair explosion.
"But the evidence is certainly not moving in the direction of a terrorist attack," he said. "It is in fact moving in the other direction."

In two other interviews, James Kallstrom, head of the FBI in New York, said theories that a bomb or a missile blew up the plane appeared less likely. Kallstrom made his remarks on NBC's "News Forum" and separately in an interview with the New York Times in its Sunday edition.

In its statement, St. Louis-based TWA said, "Suggestions of mechanical malfunction as the cause are unproven speculation and no evidence recovered to date would conclusively support such a theory ... TWA hopes that as the investigation continues to move forward, those following the investigation will remain open-minded and patient."

The Paris-bound Boeing 747, operated by TWA, exploded shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy Airport on July 17, 1996. It plunged into the Atlantic Ocean off of Long Island, New York, killing all 230 people aboard.
